thread.title: ASIA MARKETS: Asia Stocks: Nikkei Flirts With 23,000 But Can't Hang On

author: morningstar.com
title: ASIA MARKETS: Asia Stocks: Nikkei Flirts With 23,000 But Can't Hang On
text:
By Dow Jones Newswire
Finally, a 32-session losing streak ends for this Chinese stock
Asian stock markets ended generally weaker, though Japanese equities pulled off a small gain to notch the benchmark's eighth straight day of gains.
After surging nearly 1% in morning trading and briefly breached the 23,000 level, the Nikkei gave up most of those gains. It closed up just 0.1% at 22,869.50, its highest close since mid-June. This is the index's longest winning streak since Oct. 24, 2017, when the market rose for 16 straight days. With one day of trading left in August, the index is up 1.4% for the month and on track for its third straight monthly gain. For the year, it is up 0.5%.
The dollar rose to Yen111.61 from around Yen117.15 at the end of Tokyo stock trading Wednesday. That helped export-reliant names, with Sony (6758.TO) rising 0.8% and hitting a fresh 11-year intraday high and Nintendo (7974.TO) gaining 1.9%.
Hong Kong stocks slipped, finally taking a break after three days of gains. The Hang Seng shed 0.9% to 28,164.05. Vehicle manufacturer BYD (1211.HK), in which Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway(BRKA) (BRKA) has a stake, dropped 3% after reporting a 72% plunge in first-half earnings and signaling continued struggles.
The index is down 1.5% this month and is on track for its fourth straight monthly decline. It has slumped 5.9% so far this year.
Stocks in China fell, with the Shanghai Composite declining 1.1%, its third straight loss, to close at 2,737.74. The Shenzhen Composite lost 1.5%. But troubled vaccine maker Changsheng Biotechnology(002680.SZ) finally snapped its record 32-session losing streak by logging a limit-up 5% gain. Even so, it's down 86% from just before the plunge began.
Taiwan's Taiex edged down fractionally. Stocks in suppliers of Apple Inc. (AAPL) iPhone components were mixed following a report by Loup Ventures that upcoming U.S. iPhone sales could be 3% stronger than expected. Taiwan Semiconductor (2330.TW) gained 1.7%, but Foxconn (2354.TW) and Largan Precision Co. (3008.TW) each lost 0.3%.
South Korea's Kospi edged down 0.1%. A report that the Trump administration had allowed targeted relief from some U.S. steel and aluminum quotas (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-grants-steel-aluminum-relief-for-some-trade-partners-report-2018-08-29) boosted shares of steelmakers Hyundai Steel (004020.SE), up 0.6%, and Posco (PKX), up 0.3%.
Australia's ASX 200 narrowly lost ground after Wednesday's 10 1/2 -year closing high, thanks to a last-hour slide, while New Zealand slipped after another record close Wednesday. Benchmarks in Southeast Asia were mixed, with declines in Singapore and Malaysia , but gains in Indonesia .
